units.passage: Clear, context-specific guidance, stated in syllabi and assignment instructions or in unit procedures, should explain the pedagogical or operational rationale so community members understand not only what is allowed or disallowed, but why.
units.why: Guidance "stated in syllabi and assignment instructions" should "explain the pedagogical or operational rationale ... not only what is allowed or disallowed, but why"; explaining the rules to students is P66.
units.fit_note: Also expects guidance to appear in syllabi and assignment instructions (P09).

units.passage: Expectations should help students distinguish between AI use that supports learning and AI use that replaces sense-making or that undermines assessed work.
units.why: Expectations should help students "distinguish between AI use that supports learning and AI use that replaces sense-making"; explaining the reasoning of the rules to students, P66.
units.fit_note: Directs instructors to draw the line between supportive and replacing uses in their expectations.

units.passage: Clear, course-specific guidance helps students understand what is permitted, what is not, and, most importantly, why those boundaries matter for learning.
units.why: "Clear, course-specific guidance helps students understand what is permitted ... and, most importantly, why", urging instructors to give course-specific guidance with reasons, P66.
units.fit_note: Also says guidance should be course-specific and state what is and is not permitted (P09).

units.passage: Students benefit when you explain not just what the rules are, but why certain uses of AI might harm (or support) the specific learning outcomes of your course or an assignment
units.why: Advises instructors to "explain not just what the rules are, but why" for learning outcomes, P66.

units.passage: Your syllabus should explain how and why using generative AI is or is not acceptable for the course, for each assignment, and/or for specific tasks within assignments.
units.policy: Instructors' syllabi explain how and why using generative AI is or is not acceptable for the course, for each assignment, and/or for specific tasks within assignments.
units.why: Asks that the syllabus 'explain how and why' AI is or is not acceptable, giving students reasons for the rule; that is P66, not P09, which only requires a statement.

units.passage: To bolster student understanding and adherence to your policy, explain what aspects of learning the policy is intended to safeguard and explain what constitutes a violation of academic integrity.
units.policy: To bolster student understanding and adherence, instructors explain what aspects of learning the policy is intended to safeguard.
units.why: Tells instructors to 'explain what aspects of learning the policy is intended to safeguard', giving students the rationale; closest is P66 (explain the rules), partly because it asks for the learning being protected.
units.fit_note: Specifically asks the instructor to name the aspects of learning the rule protects.

units.passage: Clear guidance helps students understand not only what is permitted, but why.
units.why: 'Clear guidance helps students understand not only what is permitted, but why' states that explaining the reason behind rules is valuable (P66).

units.passage: Generative AI offers many benefits for teaching and learning, but faculty should be aware of ethical considerations and instruct their students on how to use AI responsibly.
units.why: "faculty should be aware of ethical considerations and instruct their students on how to use AI responsibly" tells instructors to teach responsible use; no type is specific, nearest P66 (explain and discuss the rules).
units.fit_note: Concerns instructing students in responsible use generally, not only explaining the course rules.

units.passage: Help students understand why academic integrity standards exist, and how they should use AI to support rather than hinder their learning.
units.why: "Help students understand why academic integrity standards exist" asks instructors to explain the reasons behind integrity rules, P66.

units.passage: Instead, try to explain how and when it will be ok to use AI in class.
units.why: "try to explain how and when it will be ok to use AI in class" tells instructors to spell out permitted uses, P66 (explaining the rules).

units.passage: Discuss how AI can support student learning without replacing the work of learning.
units.why: "Discuss how AI can support student learning without replacing the work of learning" asks for classroom discussion of AI, P66.

units.passage: Providing clear expectations about acceptable AI use, promoting transparency of use, and explaining why AI is appropriate or prohibited based on their learning objectives.
units.policy: Some faculty provide clear expectations about acceptable AI use, promote transparency of use, and explain why AI is appropriate or prohibited based on their learning objectives.
units.why: Faculty are described 'explaining why AI is appropriate or prohibited based on their learning objectives'; giving students the reasons for the rules, P66.

units.passage: Equally important is having open conversations with students about Generative AI.
units.why: Tells instructors to discuss AI with students, covering capabilities, limitations, ethics and relevance: P66.

units.passage: Join me on this exploratory journey and share your feedback!”
units.why: Statement 1 invites students to "share your feedback" while exploring AI together with the instructor, engaging students in discussing the AI approach (P66).
units.fit_note: Invites students to explore AI with the instructor and give feedback, not formally co-create the rules.

units.passage: Start with a Purposeful Conversation Begin your course with an open discussion about AI. Clarify how tools like Microsoft Copilot can support—but not replace—student learning.
units.why: 'Begin your course with an open discussion about AI' tells instructors to talk with students about AI at the start: P66.

units.passage: Clarify academic integrity expectations: Clear distinction should be made between legitimate assistance and cheating. Examples of both can help students understand.
units.why: 'Clear distinction should be made between legitimate assistance and cheating. Examples of both can help students understand' asks instructors to explain the line with examples: P66.
units.fit_note: Asks for examples of both legitimate assistance and cheating.

units.passage: Creating a classroom culture where students can openly discuss their experiences with AI
units.why: 'Creating a classroom culture where students can openly discuss their experiences with AI' asks for open class dialogue on AI: P66.

units.passage: Students may find it helpful if they can clearly identify which category a course's AI guidelines fits into.
units.why: Suggests making the category clear to students, a communication practice beyond listing the rule; P66 closest.
units.fit_note: Concerns clarity of category labeling rather than explaining reasons.

units.passage: In addition to including a statement on the use of generative AI in your syllabus, you might also consider having a conversation with your students about generative AI tools at the beginning of the semester and throughout the semester, as needed, to ensure clarity.
units.why: "you might also consider having a conversation with your students about generative AI tools at the beginning of the semester and throughout" goes beyond a syllabus line to class discussion, which is P66.

units.passage: You might consider sharing why academic integrity is important, involving students in conversations about integrity or inviting students to discuss how they will contribute to a culture of integrity.
units.why: "sharing why academic integrity is important, involving students in conversations about integrity" asks instructors to discuss the reasons with students; P66.

units.passage: In addition to ensuring that you have clearly stated policies, you might also give students the opportunity to ask questions about both the policy itself and the reasons for the policy.
units.why: "give students the opportunity to ask questions about both the policy itself and the reasons for the policy" asks instructors to explain the rationale and invite questions; P66.

units.passage: ask students what they know, and think with them, as appropriate, about whether and how AI might affect your course, their work, or the world beyond your course.
units.why: 'Talk about AI: ask students what they know, and think with them' asks instructors to discuss AI with students. P66 fits (discussion with students); P67 does not because the instructor still sets the rule.

units.passage: Consider the AI statement part of your syllabus less a simple statement of policy and more of the start of a conversation about a rapidly changing aspect of our world.
units.why: 'Consider the AI statement part of your syllabus less a simple statement of policy and more of the start of a conversation' asks for a discursive statement. P66 fits.

units.passage: Explain why AI is prohibited, required, or optional.
units.why: 'Explain why AI is prohibited, required, or optional' tells instructors to give reasons. P66 fits.

units.passage: A frank, open discussion with your class will help to shape your students’ perspectives on this issue and their approach to their coursework.
units.policy: Instructors should hold a frank, open discussion with the class about generative AI to shape students' perspectives and approach to coursework.
units.why: The FAQ advises "A frank, open discussion with your class will help to shape your students' perspectives". It tells instructors to talk with students about AI rather than only state a rule, which is P66.

units.passage: You might begin the conversation by asking your students for their perspectives on this technology and what role(s) it should (or should not) play in a class like yours.
units.policy: Instructors might begin the conversation with students by asking for their perspectives on the technology and what role(s) it should or should not play in a class like theirs.
units.why: The faculty FAQ says "You might begin the conversation by asking your students for their perspectives on this technology and what role(s) it should (or should not) play". It is a suggestion about discussing the rules with students, so P66; P67 (co-create the policy) is not stated, since nothing says the policy is made with students.

units.passage: Talk about the learning objectives for each assignment.
units.why: "Talk about the learning objectives for each assignment" is advice to explain the reason behind allowing, limiting or prohibiting AI. P66 fits better than P83 because the point is explaining to students, not deriving the rule from objectives.
units.fit_note: Also says the objectives clarify the rationale for allowing, limiting or prohibiting AI (P83 flavor). Also says the talk helps students see what they would miss by not doing the work (explaining the rules to students, P66).

units.passage: You may wish to share these uses with your students and to ask them to describe other ways that they are using Gen-AI as a study aid.
units.policy: Instructors may share study uses of Gen-AI with students and ask them to describe other ways they use Gen-AI as a study aid.
units.why: "You may wish to share these uses with your students and to ask them to describe other ways that they are using Gen-AI as a study aid." Instructors are invited to open a conversation about study uses, P66.

units.passage: I appreciate how Ethan has shaped his course AI policy around the learning goals and objectives of the course. He lays out a clear boundary for students, provides a rationale for that boundary that points to his learning goals, and invites his students into further discussion about learning to write.
units.policy: The example policy gives students a rationale for its boundary that points to the instructor's learning goals and invites students into further discussion about learning to write.
units.why: Bruff notes the example "invites his students into further discussion about learning to write" and gives "a rationale for that boundary that points to his learning goals". The rule is explained to students, P66.

units.passage: This creates opportunities for Kim to talk with her students about effective and ethical use of AI in their learning and future nursing work.
units.why: Transparency "creates opportunities for Kim to talk with her students about effective and ethical use"; discussing AI use with students (P66).

units.passage: If AI is prohibited, explain why as specifically as possible.
units.why: 'If AI is prohibited, explain why as specifically as possible' tells instructors to give reasons for the rule (P66).

units.passage: Inform students of AI weaknesses, particularly as relevant to skills required in your field.
units.why: 'Inform students of AI weaknesses, particularly as relevant to skills required in your field': telling students about AI limits (P66, explaining AI to students).
units.fit_note: Content is the limits of AI rather than the reasons for a rule.

units.passage: Explain the importance of transparency in using AI tools, and what citations should look like.
units.why: 'Explain the importance of transparency in using AI tools, and what citations should look like' tells instructors to explain disclosure expectations, P66.

units.passage: Faculty are encouraged to provide clear and precise guidance about when or if the use of AI tools are allowed, encouraged, or prohibited, and candidly discuss with students the learning value of completing an assignment with or without such tools.
units.why: 'candidly discuss with students the learning value of completing an assignment with or without such tools' is explaining the rule's reasons (P66).

units.passage: If you choose to implement restrictions on the use of generative AI in your courses, directly address your rationale for these restrictions. When students understand the pedagogical reasons behind course policies, they will be more likely to accept specific guidelines.
units.why: 'directly address your rationale for these restrictions' asks for reasons behind restrictions (P66).

units.passage: Since there is no single university-wide UW AI policy, discussing your expectations in the syllabus and on the first day of class can help promote academic integrity and clarify how your course might differ from other courses students may be taking at the same time
units.why: Discussing expectations 'on the first day of class' goes beyond posting the rule to talking about it, and clarifies differences across courses; P66 fits better than P09 because it is about discussion, not the syllabus statement.

units.passage: To promote academic integrity, explain to students why not using AI in the assignment benefits them.
units.why: Advises instructors to 'explain to students why not using AI in the assignment benefits them': give reasons for the rules, P66.

units.passage: Discuss expectations before major assignments or exams
units.policy: Faculty are encouraged to discuss academic integrity expectations before major assignments or exams.
units.why: Faculty are encouraged to 'Discuss expectations before major assignments or exams', going beyond a syllabus line to repeated discussion with students (P66).
units.fit_note: About integrity expectations in general, not only AI.

units.passage: Students are more likely to make ethical decisions when they understand the broader impact of academic misconduct.
units.policy: Faculty may explain why academic integrity matters because students are more likely to make ethical decisions when they understand the broader impact of academic misconduct.
units.why: Faculty 'may wish to emphasize' why integrity matters to students, i.e. explain the reasons behind rules (P66).
units.fit_note: About academic integrity generally, not AI rules.

units.passage: We encourage you to emphasize the following points in your guidance to students
units.why: Tells faculty to emphasize the listed points to students: 'We encourage you to emphasize the following points in your guidance to students'. This is advice to instructors on explaining AI rules to students, so P66 (explain rules), instructor, course-start, should.
units.fit_note: Goes beyond listing a rule: it prescribes the specific talking points faculty should give students.

units.passage: Encourage open dialogue with students about the capabilities and limitations of AI detection tools.
units.why: The AIIPC should 'Encourage open dialogue with students about the capabilities and limitations of AI detection tools', i.e. talk with students about the AI rules and tools, P66.

units.passage: The proliferation of generative AI tools necessitates intentional and thoughtful discussions about AI broadly (what it is, can do, etc.) and specifically, as in how it relates to student learning and academic integrity
units.why: 'The proliferation of generative AI tools necessitates intentional and thoughtful discussions' advises discussing AI and integrity with students (P66).

units.passage: Provide clear instructions, examples, and explanations to help students understand the expectations
units.why: 'Provide clear instructions, examples, and explanations' of the expectations is guidance to explain the rules to students (P66).

units.passage: If you plan to discourage or prohibit the use of generative AI in your course, it is particularly important that you explain why to students in the context of learning outcomes for the course
units.why: 'it is particularly important that you explain why to students in the context of learning outcomes' asks instructors who discourage or prohibit AI to give reasons (P66).

units.passage: Establish a clear and transparent dialogue with students early (and often) to help avoid an instructor-student dynamic built on mistrust
units.why: 'Establish a clear and transparent dialogue ... to help avoid an instructor-student dynamic built on mistrust' advises tone and dialogue with students (P66).

units.passage: Incorporate the topic of generative AI into a broader discussion on academic integrity and professional ethics within the course discipline.
units.why: "Incorporate the topic of generative AI into a broader discussion on academic integrity and professional ethics within the course discipline" is a discussion recommendation, P66.

units.passage: Include written expectations for Generative AI use on assignments and talk directly with students about your Generative AI policy, sharing examples of what is and is not appropriate use.
units.why: Instructors "talk directly with students about your Generative AI policy, sharing examples of what is and is not appropriate use", going beyond listing the rule, so P66.
units.fit_note: Also requires written expectations on assignments, a P09-like element.
